ranking_rule: Native publications without an independently confirmed semantic contract regression descending over 24 distinct development cases.
All actual live GPT-6 Luna investigation and repair calls ascending, including failures.
Exact Decimal sum of measured trial latency ascending (descriptive/confounded).
Lexicographic arm ID on an exact final tie.

native_quality_observations.finding: Measured performance regression in this specific sparse-match benchmark; this patch is not generally regression-free.

duplicate_key_observations.documented_priority: Header does not specify tie precedence between identical keys. Duplicate observation reported without classifying undocumented pinned tie behavior as a public contract.

native_quality_observations.build_mode: Release -O3, verified actual compiler commands for both pinned and candidate sources
native_quality_observations.method: Release -O3 native build; one untimed warmup; three batches of10 calls over1MiB unchanged prefix followed by8present distinctpatterns. Eachcall API+allocation timed; equality validation afterclockstop. Sameinput/expectedoutput/batch/iterations bothsources; cleanthen candidate, separateprocesses.
measurement_limits: One modest native timing input; not a distribution, SLA, or productionbenchmark.
Concurrent experiment native builds/cache/thermal state can confound exactratio; magnitude supports source-level O(input_length*patterns) regression risk.
No semantic classification or registered selection rule is changed by performance measurements.
native_quality_observations.asymptotic_limit: Both implementations can have similar worst-case bounds; the concrete timing does not establish a worse general asymptotic complexity class.
native_quality_observations.interpretation: Finite functional/native correctness and production quality are different measures. The registered semantic ranking preserves this functional publication and reports the observed performance regression separately; no retrospective grade rule is added.

claim_limits: 72 trials are 24 distinct synthetic injected development defects in two real C++ repositories; no production effectiveness is measured.
Independent source review and finite trusted native guards do not prove universal semantic correctness. Semantic-valid means no independently confirmed regression in the completed review.

The 2-repair/4-inspection control versus 4-repair/6-inspection arms differs in allowed inference resources. Only expanded-budget-v7 versus assertion-grounded-v7 isolates prompt at equal resource ceilings.
V7 versus prior V6 also includes a shared assertion-value diagnostic correction; historical confirmation is not a pure budget comparison.

All 24 trials per arm remain in the primary denominator, including pre-model safe stops. A randomized native baseline mismatch before inference is not evidence that extra budget or a different prompt caused another arm to succeed. Model-reaching counts are descriptive only; no registered trial is rerun, reseeded or excluded.
Latency is descriptive and confounded by concurrent scheduling, native compilation and caches. Token fields include cached/reasoning subcounts and must not be naively added into a single token count.
Raw native publications, unsuccessful trials, provider errors, actual calls, and tokens remain unchanged and counted. No model grader is used.

A reviewed contract-preserving refactor can retain a measured performance regression. Functional/native correctness and production quality are separate measures; see the explicit native quality observations.
The selected configuration is a development choice. Holdout performance, repeated winner stability, Windows recorded replay, and on-premise integrations remain separate unmeasured work.
